newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian IT provider Systemat to tap bourse.
newsitem.headline: Belgian IT provider Systemat to tap bourse.

text.p: Belgian hi-tech firm Systemat NV, an information technology services provider with strong growth ambitions, plans to list 49 percent of its capital on the Brussels bourse from March 26.

The third company this year to come to the market, Systemat will be tapping investors for some 240 million francs, almost two-thirds of which will go towards expanding its technical centre, co-founder Jean-Claude Loge said on Friday.
The remainder will be used to finance supplies and future growth.
Systemat, which says it is the market leader in Belgium, wants to raise sales to five billion francs in 1998 from an estimated 4.2 billion in 1997 and 3.4 in 1996.
"We will grow faster than the market," Loge told a news conference on the initial public offering.
Net profit at the company for 1998 is forecast at 140 million francs, up from an expected 100 million in 1997 and 76 million in 1996. "The first few months of 1997 are encouraging," he said.

The company, founded in 1984, offers hardware, configuration, assembly, installation, training and support services. Loge said it aims to raise its net margin to three percent by 2000, which would be 50 percent above current levels, as a result of increased sales.
"Sales will grow faster than costs...there are economies of scale...the structure is in place," Loge said.
Systemat would start paying dividends in 1997 with the payout ratio likely to be around 20 percent, or around 20 million francs, he said.
That is some 15 francs per share after the capital increase following the listing which will raise the number of outstanding shares to 1,271,120.
Systemat will list 204,480 new shares and 418,400 existing shares on the first, twice daily fixing, market of the bourse.

The shares will be priced at 1,175 francs each, representing a four percent discount to an average price calculated using a mix of the dividend discount method, discounted free cash flows and a comparison of price/expected earnings ratios (P/Es).
A study by Vermeulen Raemdonck, the brokerage of bank BBL which is lead-managing the offering, put Systemat's estimated 1997 P/E at 14.9 and 11.2 for 1998.
Compared with international competitors such as Inacom of the U.S. with a 1998 P/E of 9.8 and the U.K.'s Electrocomponent with a P/E of 20.4 Systemat would be in the middle of the range.
And compared with an estimated P/E of 14.3 for the Belgian market Systemat was relatively cheap, Vermeulen Raemdonck said.

The brokerage expected Systemat to continue to benefit from its membership of the International Computer Group (ICG), a global organisation of computer systems and network providers who have teamed up to facilitate international integration for their multinational clients.
ICG membership enables firms like Systemat to claim favourable purchasing conditions from suppliers.
The share offer opens on March 17 and runs until March 21.
